A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UNITE and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The retained material can be reliably matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation, articulation, and ablation results, with additional runtime, depth-estimation, and Replica evaluations in its appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds quantitative LERF search evaluation, view-count experiments, clustering sensitivity examples, and outdoor predictions.

M1.justification: The VGGT backbone, task-specific DPT heads, distillation and contrastive objectives, and confidence-weighted consistency losses are retained. Naming OpenSeg and clarifying separate translation/rotation outputs in v3's main text reconcile details already documented in v1 Appendix A.

E1.justification: v3 adds qualitative outdoor testing on Tanks and Temples in Appendix H, extending the previously indoor coverage. The core indoor datasets and tasks remain; LERF already appeared as a kitchen case study in v1 and receives broader scene/query evaluation in v3.

E2.justification: v3 adds IGGT to the semantic and instance comparisons in Tables 1–2 and removes OV3D from Table 1. The new search comparison includes LERF alongside existing comparators Pe3R and PanSt3R. Most previous comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Added protocols include LERF evaluation on four scenes with five queries each, segmentation mIoU and softmax-normalized cosine scores, and a ScanNet ablation using 50/100/150/200 equidistantly sampled frames. Existing training budgets and benchmark metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test scene coverage versus input-view count, HDBSCAN clustering sensitivity, and indoor-to-outdoor generalization failures (Appendices C, G, and H; Table 7; Figures 6–7). These substantially broaden robustness assessment. The articulation multi-task comparison and geometry–semantic synergy ablation already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The learned confidence maps concern model predictions, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds LERF results, including reported average mIoU of 41.7 versus Pe3R's 41.4, and view-count results ranging from 29.9 mIoU with 50 frames to 48.7 with 200. It also adds IGGT comparisons and outdoor failure findings while removing OV3D results. Matched original numerical entries, including runtime, depth, and Replica results, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 retain the same mathematical content. Added attribution and explanations for confidence weighting and stop-gradient introduce no new derivations, assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions narrow the scope to dense indoor semantics, remove explicit affordance claims from those passages, and qualify comparisons as involving zero-shot feed-forward models. The central claims about unified prediction, distillation, and multi-view consistency remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive limitations concerning outdoor domain shift, unseen concepts, object scale, and clustering sensitivity. It acknowledges lower articulation recall than S2M, offers a precision–recall interpretation, and discusses frame-coverage saturation and privacy implications. The previous explanation of the performance gap against OV3D is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies reduction from approximately 34 million points to 200,000, greedy distance-based feature aggregation, many-to-one nearest-neighbor matching, and evaluation against raw benchmark clouds. It explicitly documents ground-truth depth/pose use in Tables 1–2; Appendix G identifies ScanNet training data for clustering-parameter tuning. These disclosures do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v3 identifies already-cited IGGT as the closest approach instead of PanSt3R and expands their methodological comparison. It adds SIU3R and attribution for confidence learning and stop-gradient, while removing the OV3D reference. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction–method–experiments–conclusion structure and much existing prose remain. Local revisions clarify terminology and claims, insert a dedicated search subsection, expand the appendix roadmap, and update author/header information and citation style.

P2.justification: The two-column layout becomes a single-column TMLR layout, with substantially reformatted tables and relocated figures. v3 adds search and view-count tables, clustering and outdoor figures, and expanded evaluation captions. Table 10 additionally redisplays IGGT comparisons already included in Tables 1–2.

improvement.justification: Quantitative search evaluation, sensitivity analyses, explicit outdoor failures, and clearer evaluation details improve validation and transparency beyond v1's largely positive generalization evidence. The gain is limited by removal of OV3D's stronger ScanNet comparison and overstatement of the new LERF findings: Table 4 shows UNITE also trailing LERF on ramen and tying PanSt3R on kitchen. Overall, the added evidence and clearer applicability boundaries provide a modest quality improvement.
